data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A compliant checklist is a fixed, rigid proxy; a genuinely reliable one is a dynamic, robust tracker.","The panel may achieve compliance without understanding; the expert may have understanding without explicit compliance."],"overturn_conditions":["If the evaluation demonstrates that the panel's accuracy is invariant under perturbations that change the cue-answer mapping, the mere-compliance hypothesis is overturned."],"shared_structure":["Both systems face a distinction between superficial and deep tracking of the target variable.","Both are vulnerable to Goodhart's law when the proxy becomes the target.","Both can be distinguished by stress-testing under distribution shift."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["The compliance/reliability distinction transfers: it is not enough that the panel gets the right answer on the evaluation; it must get the right answer for the right reason."]},"claim":"The apparent reliability gain of checklist-driven panels is often mere compliance: the panel tracks the checklist's cues, which happen to correlate with the right answer within the evaluation, but this does not constitute a genuine reliability gain because it is fragile to distribution shift and does not reflect understanding.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the checklist cues are causally necessary features of the answer, compliance and reliability coincide.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the evaluation includes an out-of-distribution probe, a compliant panel will fail and a reliable panel will not.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's intuition also relies on the same cues, the panel offers no marginal reliability gain over the expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A compliant panel produces outputs that are a function of the cue structure specified by the checklist. If those cues are valid in the evaluation sample, the panel scores well. However, this is a form of overfitting to the checklist's particular cue-answer mapping. Genuine reliability requires that the panel's output be a function of the underlying answer-generating structure, which allows robustness under distribution shift.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
